title: Telemetry contract enforcement and cost-aware retention for console usage analytics
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Define and implement a telemetry contract enforcement layer between Console backend services and the usage analytics ingest pipeline, and introduce cost-aware retention tiers. This ticket covers schema contracts, CI preflight checks, runtime guards for malformed or high-volume event producers, adaptive retention policies tied to SLO/usage signals, and dashboard templates to expose economic impact. Goal: prevent silent telemetry drift that causes analytics regressions or unexpected ingestion bills, while giving teams safe default retention and an easy on-ramp to longer retention where justified.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry contract spec published and linked in Console engineering docs (schema, required fields, semantic versioning rules).
CI check (unit + contract test) added to Console services repo that fails on incompatible telemetry changes.
Ingest-side enforcement: the analytics ingest service rejects or tags events violating contracts and emits a well-defined metric and tracing span for each rejection.
Adaptive retention policy implemented: events are classified into retention tiers (ephemeral-7d, standard-30d, long-90d) by contract fields and SLO labels.
Cost dashboard panels created in Console Console Analytics showing retention tier distribution, per-tenant ingestion cost, and projected monthly spend with 95th percentile.
Runbook entries for contract drift alerts and steps for rollback or remediation.
implementation_notes: Telemetry contract: JSON Schema v2019-09 with a service-level header (service, route, version, event_type, trace_id, user_id optional). Use semantic versioning for contract updates and a compatibility matrix in the docs.

CI preflight: add a job that loads the published schema and validates sample payloads from each service. Failure should block merges that change telemetry shape unless an opt-in compatibility bump PR is present. Link to pattern: https://confluence.redwood.ai/console/telemetry-contracts

Ingest enforcement: introduce an "ingest.validation" span and two metrics: analytics.ingest.rejected_count and analytics.ingest.reject_reasons (tagged by reason). Rejections should be non-fatal by default (tagged & routed to quarantine) during rollout and treated as fatal after 2-week opt-in period per service.

Adaptive retention: retention classification runs as part of ingest pipeline transform. Default mapping: critical_events -> long-90d, session_events -> standard-30d, debug/heartbeat -> ephemeral-7d. Teams can request overrides via a retention proposal linked in docs and must provide business justification and cost estimate.

Sampling and trace linkage: preserved trace_id for sampled events; if high-volume producers exceed a per-minute threshold, the producer receives a backpressure metric and a recommended sampling policy is auto-suggested. Implement token-bucket limiter per-producer id with metrics for throttles.

Cost model: add an internal estimate metric tokens.byte_cost and tokens.retention_cost used by the cost dashboard. Use historical ingestion sizes to forecast monthly spend at current retention policy.

Observability: create dashboard templates (Grafana/Metabase) for retention tier heatmaps, top producers by cost, contract violation heatmap by service, and a drift detection alert that compares schema versions across deployments.
Rollout: staged rollout plan with quarantine mode -> opt-in grace window (2w) -> enforce mode. Provide a migration guide and example backward-compatible shim for common breaking changes.
